title: Why a stolen code is useless
goal: A public app signs a user in without holding a secret.
obstacle: Anything that crosses the browser can be intercepted, including the one-time code.
control: The client commits to a verifier hash first; only the holder of the verifier can redeem the code.

steps.title: Commit
steps.tell: The client hashes a random verifier and sends only the hash.
steps.say: We send the fingerprint, not the secret.
steps.why: An intercepted code cannot be redeemed without the verifier.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.tell: The user authenticates and approves at the authorization server.
steps.say: The user proves who they are to the server, never to the app.
steps.why: The app never sees the password.

steps.title: Redeem
steps.tell: The client sends the code and the verifier; the server checks the hash.
steps.say: Only the real client can finish the trade.
steps.why: The check ties the code to the client that asked.
